narrative.overview: SwiftMed behaves like a good pharmacist at the counter: clear, kind and exact. Every screen answers the patient's question first (where the medicine is, how far away, how sure we are), in plain words and steady type, and keeps everything else quiet. It is the category standard for a consumer health app, executed at the craft level of Zocdoc and One Medical, with SwiftMed's teal as its one voice.
keyCharacteristics: One accent (teal); state colours only where they mean something.
Figtree throughout, with tabular figures for distance, price, stock, code and time.
Labels always visible above fields; large body text (17px) for older readers.
Two radii: 10px controls, 16px panels; chips are full pills.
Soft depth tinted toward the teal; one authored motion (the code settling into place).

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Teal is the only accent. Green, amber, red and blue appear only to state freshness, hold state, an error or a notice, never as decoration.

rules.name: The Tested Pair Rule
rules.body: Every text and colour pairing is listed in web/patient-app/lib/contrast.test.ts and must pass WCAG AA. A new token is not done until its pairs are added there.

rules.name: The Counted Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number a patient compares or reads out (distance, price, stock, code, time left) is set in tabular lining figures.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Headings speak for themselves. No small uppercase tracked labels above them.

rules.name: The No Nested Cards Rule
rules.body: A panel never holds another panel. Inside a panel, group with hairline dividers and tinted rows.

dos: Do answer first: distance, price, stock and freshness are visible on every result without opening anything.
Do keep labels visible above every field and pair every icon with words.
Do keep touch targets at least 44px and body text at 17px.
Do mark demo data, degraded services and errors in a notice, every time.
Do add new colour pairs to lib/contrast.test.ts before using them.
donts: Don't add a second accent colour or use green, amber or red decoratively.
Don't use eyebrow labels, section numbers as decoration, dot badges, or equal icon-card grids.
Don't put a panel inside a panel.
Don't add a dark theme without a use-scene reason; the code is shown at a counter in daylight.
Don't use placeholder text as a label, or text smaller than 15px for anything a patient must read.
